title: Fallback LLM Rules
purpose: Provide a compact operating contract when an assistant cannot access or fails to follow the full .ai configuration.

rules.statement: Read .ai/core-context.md, .ai/rules/universal-engineering-ruleset.json, .ai/rules/controlled-implementation.json, .ai/rules/completion-workflow.json, .ai/project-configuration.md, and .ai/requirements/requirements.json before editing when available.
If any required file is unavailable, say which file is unavailable and use the fallback contract as the controlling instruction set.
Assign or confirm a REQ-### requirement ID before work begins.
State the minimum access scope before inspecting files.
Read .ai/project-map.md before broad traversal when it is available. If it is missing or stale after structural changes, run omni map or ./omni map.
Do not read or expose .env files, private keys, certificates, credentials, database files, logs, build artifacts, dependency folders, cache directories, or anything listed in .ai/.ignore.
Do not modify unrelated files, deployment scripts, infrastructure, generated dependency folders, secrets, credentials, or local environment files.
Run relevant validation. For OmniContext workspace changes, run python3 make_ai.py doctor; when assistant entrypoint files change, run python3 make_ai.py sync.

Final output must include requirement ID and status, files changed, validation performed, documentation and changelog status, risks or follow-ups, a commit entry sentence, and pull request information.
